thread.title_full: Community mourns loss of pastor struck and killed in Alcoa - NewsBreak

author: Gregory Raucoules
title: Community mourns loss of pastor struck and killed in Alcoa - NewsBreak
text:
By Gregory Raucoules ,
11 hours ago
ALCOA, Tenn. (WATE) — Family and friends are mourning the loss of an East Tennessee pastor who died after being struck by a semi-truck in Alcoa.
Rowland Buck, 61, died following the collision early Tuesday morning near the intersection of East Hunt Road and North Wright Road. He served as a pastor at St. Mark’s Global Methodist Church in Louisville.
Jason Rowe, a friend and fellow pastor, remembered the beloved 61-year-old in an interview with 6 News.
Remembering Herbert R. Colquitt: WWII sailor’s name added to Knoxville memorial “When I heard of the death of my brother Rowland, it hurt my heart greatly,” Rowe said. “He’s been a piece of my life for a couple decades. When a piece of you is gone so quickly, it hurts kind of deep.”
From left: Rowland Buck and Jason Rowe Rowe recounted fond memories of Buck baptizing his eldest child and a trip they made together to their old seminary.
“We traveled up to our old seminary one time for a conference. We got to spend about 3-4 days together. It was like brothers. We got to eat together, we pray together, we go conference together. It was just like a brotherhood,” Rowe said.
He said Buck will be remembered as a great friend, family man, and someone who made a real community impact through the church.
▶ See more top stories on WATE.com “He was a true guy. Our community has lost a mighty warrior, a man of faith, a man who deeply loved Jesus. He walked it. He lived it and he wanted people to experience and know the peace of Christ,” he said. “He loved people that way. That’s why we see such a big response in our community of people because he was an impact maker. He impacted the lives of people, of friends. He was just a genuine person and we’ve lost good one.”
